files.lesson.md: --- order: 34 unit: models9 node: AC9M9M05 n1 uses: [AC9M8N04 n1] assumes: [AC9M8N04 n1] connection: bushwalk-time title: Set up a rate model summary: "A rate is an amount per unit. To set up a model, say what each part of the situation adds to the answer, and match the units: kilometres at a speed, and climb at its own rate." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "How long will the walk to the lookout take? The map gives the distance and the climb." --- A bushwalking rule of thumb, Naismith's rule, says walkers go about 5 km/h on level ground, plus 1 hour for every 600 m of climb ([bushwalk.com navigation FAQ](https://faq.bushwalk.com/FAQ_Navigation.htm), checked 25 October 2026). The track to the lookout is 8 km with 450 m of climb (made up for the task). How long will it take? Have a guess, and we'll come back to it at the end. ## Predict: easy numbers first ```step stage: predict insight: "Choosing a time for 10 km with 600 m of climb shows whether students add the two parts or count the climb as distance." check: type: predict q: "By Naismith's rule, how long does a walk of 10 km with 600 m of climb take?" options: - "3 hours" - "2 hours" - "2.1 hours" - "12 hours" actual: "3 hours. 10 km at 5 km/h is 2 hours, and 600 m of climb adds 1 hour more. 2.1 hours counts the climb as extra kilometres, which it isn't." ``` ## Run: the two parts ```step stage: run insight: "The model has two rates added together: time on the flat is distance ÷ 5, and time for climbing is climb ÷ 600." check: { type: number, q: "How many hours does 10 km take at 5 km/h?", answer: 2, explain: "10 ÷ 5 = 2 hours." } ``` ## Investigate: build the model ```step stage: investigate insight: "Each part of the walk has its own rate and unit, and the total is their sum: time = distance ÷ 5 + climb ÷ 600." tasks: - check: type: number q: "For the lookout walk, how many hours does the 8 km take at 5 km/h? (hours)" answer: 1.6 tolerance: 0.001 explain: "8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 hours." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $8 \\div 5$?", answer: 1.6, tolerance: 0.001, explain: "8 ÷ 5 = 1.6." } - check: type: number q: "How many hours does the 450 m of climb add? (hours, 2 decimal places)" answer: 0.75 tolerance: 0.005 explain: "450 ÷ 600 = 0.75 hours." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#kai" text: "Kai works out the lookout walk's time. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: climb-as-distance explain: "Line 3: the climb is metres of height, not kilometres of walking. It has its own rate: 600 m per hour." ``` ### Two rates ```worked \text{time} = \dfrac{\text{distance (km)}}{5} + \dfrac{\text{climb (m)}}{600} :: Naismith's rule: two parts, two units. \dfrac{8}{5} = 1.6 :: Hours for the distance. \dfrac{450}{600} = 0.75 :: Hours for the climb. 1.6 + 0.75 = 2.35 :: Total hours: about 2 hours 21 minutes. ``` ### Add the parts ### Find the mistake Read Kai's working. Which line treats the climb as distance? ## Modify: other walks ```step stage: modify insight: "Changing the distance or the climb reruns the same two parts, and the model also tells you which one matters more." tasks: - hint: ["Distance ÷ 5.", "Climb ÷ 600."] check: { type: number, q: "A walk is 5$ km with 00$ m of climb. How many hours does the rule give?", answer: 3.5, tolerance: 0.01, explain: "15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 300 ÷ 600 = 0.5, so 3.5 hours." } - hint: ["No climb: only the distance part.", "20 ÷ 5."] check: { type: number, q: "A level walk is 0$ km. How many hours does the rule give?", answer: 4, explain: "20 ÷ 5 = 4 hours, with no climb to add." } - hint: ["Compare the two parts for a steep short walk.", "2 ÷ 5 and 900 ÷ 600."] check: { type: question, q: "A track is $ km long but climbs 00$ m. Which part of the time is bigger?", options: ["The climb: 1.5 hours against 0.4 hours", "The distance: it has a rate of 5", "They are equal", "Can't tell"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "0.4 hours for the distance is less than 1.5 for the climb.", "1.5 and 0.4 aren't equal.", "You can work out both."], explain: "2 ÷ 5 = 0.4 hours, 900 ÷ 600 = 1.5 hours: for steep tracks the climb dominates." } ``` ### A longer walk ### A level walk ### A steep track ## Practise: set up and use the model ```step stage: practise insight: "Using both parts of the rule with the right units." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A walk is 12 km with no climb. How many hours? (hours)" answer: 2.4 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "12 ÷ 5 = 2.4." - check: type: number q: "A walk is 5 km with 1200 m of climb. How many hours?" answer: 3 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "5 ÷ 5 = 1 and 1200 ÷ 600 = 2, so 3 hours." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $1200 \\div 600$?", answer: 2, explain: "1200 ÷ 600 = 2." } - check: type: number q: "Review: a length is 40 cm and out by 1 cm. What is the percentage error? (%)" answer: 2.5 tolerance: 0.01 explain: "1 ÷ 40 × 100 = 2.5%." ``` ### No climb ### Steep ### Review ## Make: the lookout walk ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the lookout: build the model for the walk and say what the result means." tasks: - hint: ["8 ÷ 5 and 450 ÷ 600.", "Add them."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The lookout track is 8 km with 450 m of climb. By Naismith's rule how many hours does the walk to the lookout take? (2 decimal places. Numbers are made up for the task.)" steps: - ["distance: $8 \\div 5 = 1.6$", "hours on the flat"] - ["climb: $450 \\div 600 = 0.75$", "hours for the climb"] - ["$1.6 + 0.75 = 2.35$", "total hours"] answer: "2.35" answerLabel: "Time (hours)" tolerance: 0.01 feedback: - ["1.6", "That's only the distance part. Add the climb."] - ["2.12", "That treats the climb as 0.6 km. It has its own rate."] criteria: - "I used 5 km/h for the distance." - "I used 600 m per hour for the climb." - "I added the two parts." explain: "1.6 + 0.75 = 2.35 hours, about 2 hours 21 minutes." - check: type: question q: "Is 2.35 hours a precise answer, or a rule-of-thumb estimate?" options: ["An estimate: a rule of thumb built for walkers on good tracks", "Exact", "A measurement", "Wrong"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Rules of thumb are only approximate.", "It's a model's output, not something measured.", "It's a fair estimate, not wrong."] explain: "The rule says 'about 5 km/h'. The answer is a good first estimate, not a promise." ``` ### The time ### How sure The rule is from the [bushwalk.com navigation FAQ](https://faq.bushwalk.com/FAQ_Navigation.htm) (checked 25 October 2026). The track is made up for the task. **Also used in** - **Travel.** Journey time from a distance and a speed. - **Cooking.** Cooking time for a roast is often rate times mass plus a fixed time. - **Next lesson.** Using the model to plan when to leave. ```teacher summary: Students set up a two-part rate model for walking time and use it (AC9M9M05, node 1). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can say what each part of a model adds. - I can match each rate with its unit. - I can calculate the walking time. struggle: "Mixing the units. Ask: is the climb a distance along the track or a height?" before: > Students need Rates and ratios (Year 8). The one idea: two rates, two units, add the times. Naismith's rule: about 5 km/h on level ground plus 1 hour per 600 m of ascent (bushwalk.com navigation FAQ, checked 25 October 2026). The track is made up for the task. running: - "Predict: show of hands before the check." - "Paper: the lookout walk in Make is worked on paper first." stuck: - see: A student adds the climb to the distance. ask: Is the climb how far you walk, or how high you go? fix: How high. It has its own rate. stretch: Find a local walk on a topographic map and use the rule. support: A printed card with the two rates and their units. leads: | Continues AC9M9M05 node 1. Where it leads: Solving the model. exit: q: A track climbs 300 m. How long does the climb add by Naismith's rule? a: 0.5 hours. explain: > Naismith's rule has two rates added together: time on the flat is distance ÷ 5 and time climbing is climb ÷ 600. Match each part with its unit. ```

# Kai's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: kai
The track is 8 km with a 450 m climb. The rule is 5 km/h plus 600 m per hour of climb.
450 m is 0.45 km, so the distance is 8 + 0.45 = 8.45 km.
Time = 8.45 ÷ 5 = 1.69 hours.
# endregion
